anchor: EXP-01 · The four evidence algebras (R4) — the corpus's first genuine experiment
statement: EXP-01 tested whether a simple scalar aggregation operator (A1=max, A2=weighted mean, A3=saturating 1-prod(1-si), A4=Bayesian updating) could serve as the epistemic foundation, using a formal design under triple role (mathematician/statistician/DDD) with an adversarial property test over 7 named properties on a shared normalized evidence universe. Result: MAX fails independent corroboration; Weighted Mean fails duplicates, corroboration, and dependency; Saturating and Bayesian-like both pass all 7. Verdict: 'No simple scalar operator is sufficient as the KnowledgeOS epistemic foundation,' with the strongest single result being that 'dependency must come first' (3 apparent evidences may be 1 observation plus 2 derived representations). This is COMPUTATIONALLY TESTED — the only R4 claim class with a recorded test artifact — but established only the negative result plus property/ordering requirements, not a validated aggregation architecture (candidate survival, not selection).
